Columbia DF 1610, matrices CL 5023 and CL 5039. One 25 cm 78 rpm disc. France: Columbia Graphophone, [1934]. sources.researchNote: The BnF catalogue supplies [1934] as the issue date, reconstructed from Répertoire phonographique, 3e supplément, 1934. This is a catalogue-supported issue year, not a recording-session date or a date transcribed from the label. The record therefore retains the bracketed display while distinguishing the basis of the dating. The catalogue lists matrices CL 5023 and CL 5039 together without an explicit title-by-title assignment. It names Rossi, Chagnon and Cariven but supplies no Kaper–Jurmann composer statement. The other title is retained in the bibliographic description; no additional Kaper work is inferred merely because it appears on the same disc.

media.title: C’est ton amour — Tino Rossi, listening reference
media.description: Listening copy of “C’est ton amour”, attributed to Tino Rossi by the Internet Archive collection and associated there with Columbia DF 1610. BnF independently catalogues Rossi with Marcel Cariven’s orchestra on that disc, dated [1934], but the transferred copy and take remain unverified.

media.publicCaption: “C’est ton amour”, attributed to Tino Rossi by the Internet Archive collection. BnF independently documents Columbia DF 1610, with Marcel Cariven’s orchestra, and reconstructs its issue year as [1934]. contributions.scopeNote: Issued Tino Rossi’s recording on Columbia DF 1610.

BnF catalogues Rossi with orchestra conducted by Marcel Cariven on Columbia DF 1610. The Internet Archive collection lists the same disc and provides a listening reference; its exact source copy and take have not been independently established.
